questions.problem: Find the set of values of $w$ that satisfy $w-3\le -1$ or $5w>25.$ Express your answer in interval notation.
questions.worked_solution:
We start by solving $w-3\le -1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}w-3+3 & \le -1+3 \\ w & \le 2\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196049/assets/41894afbf397505568367e80d14e34fe2b04a2acdfd5398bd8ba41727b8c67c6.png)

Then, we solve $5w>25:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5w}{5} & >\frac{25}{5} \\ w & >5\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196049/assets/262a3e683cb8c8a67cdd58c0f138e44466c346092c7f74ec03ec1483a385056a.png)

To graph the values of $w$ that satisfy either inequality, we overlay the two graphs on the same number line:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196049/assets/95d67331522c16093207de451a33bb713b42e1418d1f4c1a7aa1ef6369a51e4b.png)

Therefore, the final solution is $w\le 2$ or $w>5.$ We can write this using interval notation as

$$
(-\infty ,2]\cup (5,\infty ).
$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}3 & <10x+8<16 \\ 3-8 & <10x<16-8 \\ -5 & <10x<8 \\ -\frac{5}{10} & <x<\frac{8}{10} \\ -\frac{1}{2} & <x<\frac{4}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196049/assets/611944fd64cf3638f0cfd4ae8f8a658496af927adc7b91f68e7aafdd36817272.png)

$$
\begin{aligned}5x-1 & >9 \\ 5x & >10 \\ x & >2\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196049/assets/8b252e1c42dcac87072a33b33460a887b6ec3bfa0d1511f05a004935df1911ca.png)

canonical_examples.problem: Find all the values of $x$ that satisfy $12x+8 > 44$ or $5x+3 \leq 28.$

We start by solving $12x+8 > 44\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}12x+8 & >44 \\ 12x & >36 \\ x & >3\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196049/assets/e9eec85ca2dd2a9fd01db97a5f281d16fd958e143e048f7ff3c5e7a87dd33f0a.png)

Then, we solve $5x+3 \leq 28\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}5x+3 & \le 28 \\ 5x & \le 25 \\ x & \le 5\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196049/assets/c9cec5cfc0e476fffe4f89f89ff0585992855e8e36fe09778029d5accd2bdc6b.png)

To graph the values of $x$ that satisfy either inequality, we overlay the two graphs on the same number line:

Therefore, the final solution is $-\infty < x < \infty.$ We can write this using interval notation as $(-\infty,\infty).$

canonical_examples.problem: Find the set of values of $x$ that satisfy $1 < 5x+6 \leq 11$ or $5x-7 > 8.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
We start by solving $1 < 5x+6 \leq 11\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & <5x+6\le 11 \\ -5 & <5x\le 5 \\ -1 & <x\le 1\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196049/assets/69948e87bc893a2461ec6e8bb77dd72e77e6d496970e31df899400c42238cd01.png)

Then, we solve $5x-7 > 8\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}5x-7 & >8 \\ 5x & >15 \\ x & >3\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196049/assets/10bb9a3bcc0b13b015649e2dae70a3ff3dcd361f46e6c545182031d6e095ad16.png)

To graph the values of $x$ that satisfy either inequality, we overlay the two graphs on the same number line:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196049/assets/84a05cd47818c9609609c2f02bd026ccadfa77c6641dff82936630bf04fbe77e.png)

Thus, the final solution is $-1 <  x \leq 1$ or $x > 3.$ We can write this using interval notation as

$$
(-1,1] \cup (3,\infty).
$$

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
Suppose we want to find all of the values of $x$ that satisfy *either* $4x+2 < 6$ *or* $2x \geq 8.$

To do this, we solve each inequality individually and then compute the union of the two solutions.

We start by solving $4x+2 < 6\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}4x+2 & <6 \\ 4x & <4 \\ x & <1\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196049/assets/0d36b8e68d9fd0b33b255502860481eeb525b60382029b17434bfb072cc39da2.png)

Then, we solve $2x \geq 8\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & \ge 8 \\ x & \ge 4\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196049/assets/edf5665b7cab7f51e3f252601a96d43c6f0cbfc64e5c9b8da81f0ef09d7b2f5a.png)

To graph the values of $x$ that satisfy either inequality, we overlay the two graphs on the same number line:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196049/assets/5c60839a626f2ba8a0fe4a24f4011af0fa52c00d79fbf80039bcfdbdf0a612c7.png)

Thus, the final solution is $x < 1$ or $x \geq 4.$ We can write this using interval notation as

$$
(-\infty, 1) \cup [4,\infty).
$$
